Risk perspective The physical impacts of climate change present significant risks to Sharda Motor Industries Limited (SMIL) and the automotive industry. Climate change-induced shift s in consumer preferences and liability issues further add to the risks.

Increased Insurance Costs: As climate change-related risks become more apparent, insurance premiums business properties and assets may rise, impacting SMIL's operating expenses. Business Continuity Costs: SMIL may incur expenses related to contingency plans and resilience measures to mitigate the impact climate-related risks on operations.

a. Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/No). If “Yes”, then coverage of the system.

Yes, SMIL has implemented an occupational health and safety management system certified to ISO 45001:2018. The system covers all SMIL’s facilities and applies to people working under the Company’s control, including permanent employees, contractual workers. It is administered through a safety committee, supported by periodic risk assessments, evaluations, and inspections across covered facilities. The effectiveness of the system is monitored on an ongoing basis to ensure compliance with applicable legal requirements and to drive continual improvement.
b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis of the entity?

SMIL identifies work related hazards and assesses associated risks through a structured Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) process applied across all facilities. On a routine basis, hazards are identified through scheduled HIRA reviews of all standard operations and processes, supported by periodic safety inspections and workplace observations conducted by designated safety officers. Each identified hazard is evaluated for severity and likelihood, prioritised, and assigned control measures in line with the hierarchy of controls. Risk assessments are reviewed and updated at defined intervals. On a non-routine basis, HIRA analysis is triggered prior to activities such as machinery breakdown and maintenance work, plant modifications or new installations, changes to processes or materials, contractor and third-party jobs, and emergency situations. Hazards arising from these activities are assessed before the work commences, and appropriate controls, work permits and safe operating procedures are put in place. The outcome of both routine and non-routine assessments feed into a periodic safety review process, through which control measures are monitored for effectiveness and improvement.
c. Whether you have processes for workers to report the work- related hazards and to remove themselves from such risks? (Yes/ No)

Yes, SMIL has established defined procedures enabling workers to report work-related hazards, unsafe conditions, or safety incidents, and to remove themselves from situations they reasonably believe to present an imminent danger. Workers can report hazards through multiple channels, including direct communication with supervisors, plant and departmental heads, the safety committee, and periodic safety meetings and reviews. Reported concerns are acted upon through timely corrective measures aimed at eliminating or mitigating the identified risk. Workers are encouraged to raise safety concerns without fear of adverse consequence.
d. Do the employees/ workers of the entity have access to non- occupational medical and healthcare services? (Yes/No)

Yes, SMIL provides its employees and workers access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services through multiple arrangements. On-site first-aid facilities are available across manufacturing locations, supported by periodic visits from a physician. Employees are covered under a group mediclaim policy, and workers are enrolled under the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) scheme, providing access to medical and healthcare benefits. In addition, SMIL conducts wellness initiatives including periodic health check-ups, screenings and preventive care. The company has arrangements with local healthcare providers for general consultations, preventive care, vaccinations, and treatment of common illnesses, with referral to specialists or hospitals for advanced care where required.
